REASONING:
Step 1 – Project framing  
- Objective: improve efficiency and access to selected administrative services in Albania.  
- Scope: regulatory reform, business‑process re‑engineering, ICT upgrades, one‑stop‑shop Citizen Service Center (CSC) in Tirana, citizen‑feedback mechanism, information campaigns and online service delivery.  
- Delivery model: Results‑Based Financing (RBF) for salaries/social‑security, Project Preparation Facility (PPF) and Technical Assistance (TA).  
- Timeline: start 26‑Aug‑2015, end 30‑Sep‑2020 (effectiveness 02‑Nov‑2015, closing 31‑Dec‑2020).  
- Budget: total cost US$74.1 M, Bank financing US$32 M (PPF US$2 M, RBF US$25 M, TA US$5 M).  
- Key stakeholders: Ministry of Finance (borrower), Ministry of State for Innovation & Public Administration (MIPA – responsible agency), ADISA (implementing agency), Prime Minister’s Delivery Unit (DU), NAIS, Inter‑Ministerial Public Services Committee (IPSC), Steering Committee, various line ministries.  
- External dependencies: EU/IPA assistance, NAIS ICT platform, telecom infrastructure, construction of CSC, procurement capacity, results‑based financing mechanisms.

Step 2 – Category sweep (risk candidates with supporting text)  

**Technical**  
- “Seven institutions … have no IT system in place.”  
- “Only 45‑50 % of the archive is digitized.”  
- “NAIS is the coordinating and regulatory authority … responsible for the Government Interoperability Platform.”  

**Financial**  
- “The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial.”  
- “Procurement risk rating is High … Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA as a newly created agency.”  
- “Disbursements under the RBF part … no disbursements will be made until DLI#5 is achieved.”  
- “GoA has limited experience with results‑based lending.”  

**Schedule**  
- “The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk.”  
- “The core features and size of this new building have not been decided … financing models are being considered.”  

**Stakeholder / Organizational**  
- “Insufficient institutional and implementation capacity of the Ministry of State for Innovation … implications for implementation.”  
- “Field level staff is likely to resist the reform.”  
- “Information posters … were hidden; telephone numbers went unattended.”  

**Political / Regulatory**  
- “Omnibus legislation … expected to be passed by the end of 2016.”  

**Environmental**  
- “Potential environmental impacts … dust and noise, waste generation, material supply, use of machinery, possible traffic and safety issues.”  

**External**  
- “Only 60 internet users per 100 people in 2013.”  

Step 3 – Evidence filter  
All listed candidates are directly quoted in the appraisal document; therefore retained.

Step 4 – Assessment & mitigation (likelihood 1‑5, impact 1‑5)  

| ID | Description | Category | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation | Evidence |
|----|-------------|----------|------------|--------|------------|----------|
| R01 | Lack of existing IT systems in seven key agencies hampers automation. | technical | 4 | 4 | Provide phased ICT capacity‑building, hire external experts, and deploy interim manual‑to‑digital processes. | “Seven institutions … have no IT system in place.” |
| R02 | Incomplete digitization of legacy registers (45‑50 % only) limits data quality. | technical | 3 | 3 | Prioritize digitization of high‑volume registers and allocate dedicated budget for scanning and validation. | “Only 45‑50 % of the archive is digitized.” |
| R03 | ADISA’s weak procurement capacity (new agency) creates high procurement risk. | organizational | 4 | 4 | Accelerate recruitment of procurement specialists, provide Bank‑led training, and use experienced consultants for early contracts. | “Procurement risk rating is High … Very weak procurement capacity at ADISA.” |
| R04 | Overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial. | financial | 3 | 4 | Implement a detailed Financial Management Manual, hire two finance specialists, and conduct regular internal audits. | “The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial.” |
| R05 | Unfinalized design and financing model for the CSC may delay construction. | schedule | 3 | 4 | Finalize architectural design and financing (PPP or public) within the first project year; set firm construction milestones. | “The core features and size of this new building have not been decided … financing models are being considered.” |
| R06 | Compressed implementation timeline may cause missed milestones. | schedule | 4 | 3 | Use results‑based incentives, monitor quarterly milestones, and allow schedule adjustments where necessary. | “The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk.” |
| R07 | Delay in passing omnibus legislation could stall regulatory reforms. | political_regulatory | 3 | 4 | Establish a legislative task‑force, engage parliament early, and align reform drafts with existing legal frameworks. | “Omnibus legislation … expected to be passed by the end of 2016.” |
| R08 | Front‑office staff may resist process re‑engineering. | stakeholder | 3 | 3 | Deploy a change‑management program with training, incentives, and clear communication of benefits. | “Field level staff is likely to resist the reform.” |
| R09 | Low internet penetration limits uptake of e‑services. | external | 4 | 3 | Set up assisted‑access points (internet cafés, community centres) and maintain non‑digital service channels. | “Only 60 internet users per 100 people in 2013.” |
| R10 | Emphasis on digital services could exclude poor and vulnerable groups. | stakeholder | 3 | 4 | Preserve physical service points, provide assisted digital access, and run targeted outreach campaigns. | “Risk that focus on state‑of‑the‑art means … will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable.” |
| R11 | Construction of the CSC may cause dust, noise, waste and traffic impacts. | environmental | 2 | 3 | Implement the Environmental Management Plan (EMP) with monitoring, dust suppression, waste management, and traffic control. | “Potential environmental impacts … dust and noise, waste generation, … traffic and safety issues.” |
| R12 | High public perception of corruption may undermine trust in new services. | stakeholder | 3 | 4 | Strengthen citizen‑feedback mechanism, publish performance data, and conduct anti‑corruption training for staff. | “Citizens still view corruption as a significant problem … bribery prevalence 19.3%.” |
| R13 | Project depends on NAIS’s capacity to integrate databases and e‑government platforms. | technical | 3 | 3 | Formalize service‑level agreements with NAIS, provide joint capacity‑building workshops, and monitor integration milestones. | “NAIS is the coordinating and regulatory authority … responsible for the Government Interoperability Platform.” |
| R14 | Government’s limited experience with results‑based financing may affect DLI achievement. | organizational | 3 | 3 | Provide dedicated RBF training, embed Bank technical assistance, and set up a DLI tracking unit within the PMU. | “GoA has limited experience with results‑based lending.” |
| R15 | PMU staffing gaps (unfilled procurement and admin positions) risk implementation delays. | organizational | 4 | 3 | Fast‑track recruitment, use interim contracts, and assign existing staff to critical tasks pending hires. | “PMU staff not yet contracted; procurement and admin specialist positions have been readvertised.” |
| R16 | Coordination among >12 ministries and agencies is complex and may cause bottlenecks. | stakeholder | 3 | 3 | Strengthen the Steering Committee, define clear RACI matrix, and hold weekly coordination meetings. | “Coordination among the different departments and agencies … complex.” |
| R17 | Failure to verify DLIs on time could delay RBF disbursements and cash flow. | financial | 3 | 4 | Build a robust M&E system with third‑party validation and automate quarterly DLI reporting. | “No disbursements under RBF will be made until DLI#5 is achieved.” |
| R18 | Manual payroll systems increase risk of errors and fraud. | financial | 3 | 3 | Deploy the new HRMIS, automate payroll processing, and conduct regular reconciliations. | “Payroll systems remain manual … extensive manual reconciliations required.” |
| R19 | Inadequate public communication may lead to low service uptake. | stakeholder | 3 | 3 | Launch a multi‑channel communication campaign (posters, SMS, radio) and monitor reach. | “Information posters … were hidden; telephone numbers went unattended.” |
| R20 | Delays in annual external audits could affect compliance reporting. | financial | 2 | 2 | Prepare audit schedules early, provide auditors with complete documentation, and track audit deliverables. | “Annual audit of EEPs due by Sep 30 2016; audit of PPF/TA due by Jun 30.” |

All risks are directly supported by statements in the provided Project Appraisal Document.

risks.description: Overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial.
risks.mitigation: Implement a detailed Financial Management Manual, hire two finance specialists, and conduct regular internal audits.
risks.evidence: The overall financial management risk is rated as Substantial.

risks.evidence: The core features and size of this new building have not been decided; financing models are being considered.

risks.mitigation: Use results‑based incentives, monitor quarterly milestones, and allow schedule adjustments where necessary.
risks.evidence: The compressed implementation timeline is a potential risk.

risks.mitigation: Establish a legislative task‑force, engage parliament early, and align reform drafts with existing legal frameworks.
risks.evidence: Omnibus legislation expected to be passed by the end of 2016.

risks.description: Front‑office staff may resist process re‑engineering.
risks.mitigation: Deploy a change‑management program with training, incentives, and clear communication of benefits.
risks.evidence: Field level staff is likely to resist the reform.

risks.description: Low internet penetration limits uptake of e‑services.
risks.mitigation: Set up assisted‑access points (internet cafés, community centres) and maintain non‑digital service channels.
risks.evidence: Only 60 internet users per 100 people in 2013.

risks.description: Emphasis on digital services could exclude poor and vulnerable groups.
risks.mitigation: Preserve physical service points, provide assisted digital access, and run targeted outreach campaigns.
risks.evidence: Risk that focus on state‑of‑the‑art means will diminish access of the poor and vulnerable.

risks.description: High public perception of corruption may undermine trust in new services.

risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated RBF training, embed Bank technical assistance, and set up a DLI tracking unit within the PMU.
risks.evidence: GoA has limited experience with results‑based lending.

risks.mitigation: Fast‑track recruitment, use interim contracts, and assign existing staff to critical tasks pending hires.
risks.evidence: PMU staff not yet contracted; procurement and admin specialist positions have been readvertised.

risks.description: Coordination among >12 ministries and agencies is complex and may cause bottlenecks.
risks.mitigation: Strengthen the Steering Committee, define a clear RACI matrix, and hold weekly coordination meetings.
risks.evidence: Coordination among the different departments and agencies involved in the Project is complex.

risks.description: Failure to verify DLIs on time could delay RBF disbursements and cash flow.
